mechanism_narrative: The sharp recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals renewed daily trip generation. As commuting and station access normalize, incidental spending near stations and offices rises, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue rising but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean within 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL time combined with stronger GROCERY_PHARM implies more local errand substitution and neighborhood circulation. That pattern supports nearby retail visits and should push RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and GROCERY_PHARM remains above baseline but RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 14 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT moves from clearly depressed levels to near baseline, access friction falls and discretionary shopping becomes easier. The first weeks after TRANSIT crosses the -5 point threshold should show a positive RETAIL_REC response.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -29.3 at t-3w to -2.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -5 but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the threshold mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and TRANSIT both rising indicates more out-of-home circulation and leisure trips that spill into shopping stops. Under that joint expansion, RETAIL_REC should trend upward over the next month.
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT rise together for another month but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls versus the prior month, reject this spillover hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PARKS mobility usually marks weakening outdoor leisure intensity and lower weekend discretionary activity. If that leisure signal persists, retail-and-recreation mobility should soften over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS keeps falling or stays deeply negative while RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES recover faster than TRANSIT, commuting is being restored through private modes rather than reduced trip generation. That split weakens retail spillovers, so RETAIL_REC should not rise as much over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES exceeds TRANSIT by at least 8 points
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains at least 8 points above TRANSIT but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rise in GROCERY_PHARM can crowd out discretionary retail by redirecting household trips toward necessity shopping. If this rise persists, retail-and-recreation mobility should lag over the next week before recovering only if the grocery surge fades.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM increased from -4.1 at t-3w to 19.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above 15 and RETAIL_REC still increases in the next week, the crowding-out mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous tightening in RESIDENTIAL and collapse in TRANSIT at the same time as WORKPLACES remain depressed indicates fewer cross-city excursions and fewer shopping opportunities. In that restricted-mobility regime, RETAIL_REC should stay below its recent average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT stays near zero and WORKPLACES remain negative, but RETAIL_REC nonetheless exceeds its prior 4-week mean, reject the hypothesis.
